Retiam features a flexible camera and viewing system designed for both mathematical 2D coordinate demonstrations and complex 3D cinematic camera choreographies.

blocks.text: The `Camera` entity extends [`Entity`](https://github.com/abhilasbiswas/Retiam/blob/main/src/engine/_core/Entity.ts) and maintains both perspective and orthographic projection models.

items: **`PERSPECTIVE`**: Models a pinhole camera with configurable Field of View (`fov` in degrees), near clipping plane (`near`), and far clipping plane (`far`).
**`ORTHOGRAPHIC`**: Models parallel projection with `orthoScale`, preserving parallel lines without perspective foreshortening (crucial for technical diagrams and UI overlays).

blocks.text: Retiam eliminates manual camera positioning guesswork by providing mathematical bounding-box framing:

items: **Bounding Volume Evaluation**: Computes the world-space Axis-Aligned Bounding Box (AABB) of the target.
**Frustum Fitting Distance**: Calculates the minimum distance required along the viewing vector so that the bounding sphere fits completely inside the camera's horizontal and vertical viewing angles:
**Physical Depth of Field Alignment**: Updates `camera.focusDist = distance` to place the sharpest focus plane exactly on the subject during raytracing.

blocks.text: Retiam provides specialized controllers for interactive exploration:

items: **Domain**: 2D coordinate spaces, vector diagrams, and board-style navigation.

children: Right-click drag or middle-click drag to pan.
Scroll wheel to zoom centered on mouse cursor position.

items: **Domain**: 3D geometric primitives, mathematical manifolds, and architectural scenes.

children: Azimuth angle ($\theta$), elevation angle ($\phi$), and distance ($r$) relative to a focal target point.

items: **Inertial Damping**: Smooth exponential decay ($e^{-\lambda \Delta t}$) on mouse release, preventing jarring motion stops.
**Constraint Limits**: Min/max polar angle clamping to prevent gimbal inversion.

blocks.text: Retiam separates the concept of a **Camera** from a **RenderView**. A scene can declare multiple simultaneous views:
Retiam uses multi-view passes to cleanly separate world-space entities from UI widgets:

children: Renders 3D/2D scene entities matching layer mask `0x7FFFFFFF`.
Uses an orthographic camera matching window pixel coordinates or normalized viewport.
**`clearDepth = true`** (clears depth buffer so UI elements never clip into 3D scene geometry).
Only processes entities with `isUI = true` (layer mask `0x80000000`).

blocks.text: By configuring two `RenderView` instances with different viewports (e.g. `[0, 0, 0.5, 1.0]` and `[0.5, 0, 0.5, 1.0]`), Retiam renders multiple synchronized camera viewpoints into a single frame buffer without performance penalty.
